questions.question: Which statement best captures the core training-data-management invariant?
options: Every model must use the newest available rows
Every dataset must fit in one storage system
Every model must resolve to an immutable manifest that resolves all training evidence
Every training run must use the same algorithm
questions.explanation: The manifest connects a model to exact sources, transformations, labels, splits, checks, and permissions.

questions.question: Why is a path such as training/latest.parquet insufficient as a dataset version?
options: Parquet cannot store labels
The path can resolve to different bytes after corrections, late arrivals, or retention changes
Only relational tables can be versioned
A dataset version must always include model weights
questions.explanation: A mutable locator does not identify the exact source state consumed by a training run.

questions.question: A 100,000-row candidate has 2.5% missing labels and 1% duplicates. Ignoring overlap, what is the upper-bound review queue?
options: 250 rows
1,000 rows
2,500 rows
3,500 rows
questions.explanation: The upper bound is 2,500 missing-label rows plus 1,000 duplicate rows, or 3,500 before overlap.

questions.question: Aggregate quality checks pass, but critical-slice coverage is below its blocking threshold. What should the release gate do?
options: Block release and investigate the critical slice
Average the slice result into the aggregate score
Release because overall volume is high
Delete the slice from evaluation
questions.explanation: A critical contract must remain independently visible; an aggregate average cannot waive it.

questions.question: Which split policy best reduces entity leakage while remaining reproducible?
options: Shuffle rows independently on every run
Move difficult evaluation rows into training
Hash a stable entity key with a recorded algorithm and seed
Sort by label and take every tenth row
questions.explanation: Stable entity-level assignment keeps related records together and makes the split repeatable.

questions.question: Two annotators disagree on a consequential example. What is the strongest data-management response?
options: Keep only the faster annotator's answer
Drop all evidence of disagreement
Treat the majority label as certain truth
Preserve votes and provenance, then route the case to adjudication
questions.explanation: Disagreement is quality evidence. Preserving it supports review, rubric repair, and uncertainty analysis.

questions.question: A source record becomes disallowed after two dataset releases and three models consumed it. What capability identifies the affected artifacts?
options: Bidirectional lineage from source records through releases and model runs
A larger training cluster
Random resampling
A model-only registry without dataset inputs
questions.explanation: Lineage traces both what produced an artifact and which downstream artifacts depend on a source.

questions.question: Why should a corrected dataset be released under a new identity instead of overwriting the old release?
options: New identities always reduce storage cost
Preserving the old identity keeps prior experiments and incidents explainable
Models cannot read updated files
Checksums work only once
questions.explanation: Immutable release identities preserve reproducibility, comparison, lineage, and incident evidence.
